subject: Business
title: The Attention Economy
description: A quick, practical guide to The Attention Economy.

hook.text: The average person sees 4,000 to 10,000 ads per day. They remember maybe three.

buildup.text: Herbert Simon warned in 1971: a wealth of information creates a poverty of attention.

discovery.text: Attention is the scarcest resource in marketing. Every brand competes for the same limited cognitive bandwidth.

twist.text: More ad spend doesn't equal more attention. People have learned to tune out anything that looks like an ad.

climax.text: The winners earn attention through value: education, entertainment, or utility — not just interruption.

punchline.text: You can't buy attention anymore. You have to earn it.

quiz.question: What did Herbert Simon warn about in 1971?
options: A wealth of information creates a poverty of attention

details.summary: The attention economy treats human attention as the scarcest resource in an information-rich world. Every brand, platform, and content creator competes for the same finite pool of consumer attention, making the ability to capture and hold attention the most valuable marketing skill.
details.whyItMatters: Consumers are bombarded with thousands of marketing messages daily but can consciously process very few. Winning in the attention economy requires cutting through noise with relevance, emotion, and formats optimized for increasingly fragmented
takeaways: Human attention is the scarcest and most contested marketing resource today
Consumers encounter thousands of messages daily but process only a tiny fraction
Capturing attention requires relevance, emotional resonance, and format innovation

faq.question: How has the attention economy changed marketing strategy?
faq.answer: Content must deliver value in seconds rather than minutes. Formats shifted from long-form to short video, stories, and reels. Headlines matter more than body copy. Personalization targets the most receptive audience. Interruption marketing is giving way to permission and pull-based approaches.

faq.question: Is the average human attention span really shrinking?
faq.answer: The popular claim that human attention spans are shorter than goldfish is largely a myth. People still binge watch series for hours. What has changed is tolerance for irrelevant content. Attention is not shorter but more selective. Interesting content gets attention;
